headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and write-capable agentic-flow can create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with Great Expectations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agentic-flow can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and shell-like tooling, while great_expectations reads and writes files in data workflows. A shared workspace or file handoff could let attacker-controlled content from agentic-flow be interpreted as instructions by Great Expectations. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty is kept at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF Great Expectations consumes agentic-flow output as configuration or documentation without sanitization
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic parsing of agentic-flow outputs by Great Expectations
Require a human review step before any generated file is treated as config
Use read-only mounts for agentic-flow outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: agentic-flow touches task prompts, repository metadata, and code, and can egress to allowlisted network destinations; Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation via files. If they share a workspace, sensitive prompts or repository data can flow into validation artifacts or outbound requests. The profiles do not show unrestricted exfiltration, so medium is the best fit.
conditions: IF both agents share files containing prompts, code, or validation results
IF agentic-flow forwards file contents through its allowlisted egress path
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared directories
Restrict agentic-flow egress to explicit destinations only
Redact prompts before writing validation artifacts
Rotate or isolate credentials used by either agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agentic-flow can execute shell commands, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Great Expectations can also install packages and operates on files. Overlapping write and environment-changing capabilities create conflict risk in a shared repo or workspace, though the profiles do not prove simultaneous unrestricted writes to the same directory. Uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout or package environment
IF either agent writes without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate virtual environments
Use a single writer for git state
Serialize package installation steps
Make one agent read-only on shared directories
requires-engineering: add file locks around mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: agentic-flow can generate outputs from background analysis tasks, and Great Expectations can consume validation results and documentation. If Great Expectations treats agentic-flow output as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated claims into downstream validation or reporting. The profiles do not show explicit verification gates, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Great Expectations ingests agentic-flow outputs as inputs to validation or reporting
IF no independent verification step checks those outputs
mitigations: Add a manual verification step before ingestion
Require schema validation on all inter-agent outputs
Keep generated claims separate from source data
Log provenance for each transferred artifact
requires-engineering: implement confidence/attestation checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch shown. The only compliance-relevant data classes are generic prompts, code, validation results, and documentation, so a concrete breach is not evidenced. Because neither profile cites a conflicting compliance regime, this remains low rather than none due to incomplete policy detail.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Document retention settings for both agents
Keep logs minimal and local
Review deployment region before use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
